title: Local and global finite Tor dimension on a quasi-compact pro-étale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme, meaning that every open cover of its underlying space has a finite subcover [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $A$ be a commutative ring. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with its pro-étale topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a site object $U$, write $M|_U$ for derived restriction to the slice ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proét}}/U,A_X|_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Derived tensor and its cohomology use [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The following are equivalent:

1. There are integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf $N$, one has $H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.
2. For every site object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $a_i\leq b_i$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X|_{U_i}$-module sheaf $N_i$ on the slice site, one has $H^q(M|_{U_i}\otimes^L_{A_X|_{U_i}}N_i)=0$ for $q\notin[a_i,b_i]$.

No boundedness, constructibility, Noetherian, or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $M$, $A$, or $X$ beyond quasi-compactness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof: making local finite Tor dimension uniform on quasi-compact X; the local-to-global argument applies to arbitrary constant coefficient module complexes. Local finite Tor dimension is Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, in sites-cohomology.tex.

proof.text: Compare the representative Tor test with the localized tensor. For a quasi-isomorphism f:F→P between K-flat complexes, its cone is acyclic and K-flat. Tensor of this cone with every complex is acyclic; signed symmetry and the tensor-cone comparison therefore make Tot(f tensor id_D) a quasi-isomorphism for every D. Resolve any K-flat representative P by a flat-term K-flat F. The first-variable representative calculation of wfSiteDerivedTensor computes tensor using F; invert the displayed quasi-isomorphism to obtain the same computation using P. The localization homology factorization identifies the resulting cohomology with ordinary complex homology. Conversely resolve a representative of an arbitrary derived M to obtain a K-flat representative. These comparisons prove coefficientModelTorAmplitude_iff_localizedTensor with exactly the same interval and arbitrary degree-zero module tests.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YT: K-flat resolutions, invariance, and computation of derived tensor; Tag 08FZ.

proof.text: Given a global interval [a,b], use the preceding comparison, apply siteTorIntervalRestriction to every slice, and compare its representative-based restriction to coefficientModelSliceRestriction. For the latter comparison use the exact module restriction functor F: the inverse of mapDerivedCategoryFactors on Q.objPreimage M followed by F.mapDerivedCategory applied to Q.objObjPreimageIso M. Transport the localized tensor and cohomology through this isomorphism, then apply the reverse representative comparison. Thus the same interval works on every slice against all slice modules. The maximal presieve on every U is covering and satisfies the local condition.

source.place: Tag 08H5, lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback, and Tags 03DH/08JB: exact slice restriction.

proof.text: For the converse cover X by finitely many affine opens. On each affine apply the local hypothesis. Transport its covering sieve from the coefficient-sized model to X.ProEt by AsSmall.down; a covering sieve contains a generating pro-etale covering family. On this affine target select finitely many affine opens in members of that family whose images cover the target. Each selected cover member factors through a member of the original presieve. Retain those original presieve members, with their given intervals: their arrows need not be affine. The finite affine refinements certify that the retained family covers. Compose over the finite affine open cover of X, transport back to the small model, and use the terminal-object characterization of CoversTop. Reindex the finite sum of finite index sets by Fin n. This is the proved helper coefficientProEtale_exists_finite_cover; no quasi-separatedness is used.

source.place: Tags 0989, 098B and 098C: affine-target finite refinements, Zariski coverings, and composition.

proof.text: Choose the interval [a_i,b_i] on each of the finitely many retained original local objects V_i. Finite.bddBelow_range and Finite.bddAbove_range provide lo≤a_i and b_i≤hi. The interval [min(lo,0),max(hi,0)] is ordered and contains all chosen intervals. If the finite family is empty, the inserted zero still makes an ordered interval. A degree outside this interval lies outside every [a_i,b_i]. Unlike passing to the affine refinements, retaining the original presieve members requires no further restriction or relocalization of their Tor intervals.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof: uniform Tor bounds on quasi-compact X.

proof.text: Fix any global K-flat representative P of M, any global module N and an integer q outside the common interval. Exact restriction to V_i preserves K-flatness. Its derived factorization sends the given Q(P)≅M to Q(P|V_i)≅M|V_i. The local interval therefore kills the homology of Tot((P|V_i) tensor (N|V_i)[0]). The natural module tensor restriction comparison, after identifying total tensor with a degree-zero second argument with the termwise tensor-right functor, identifies that complex with the restriction of Tot(P tensor N[0]). Exact restriction commutes with homology by ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso. Thus the q-th global Tor-test homology sheaf restricts to zero on every V_i. This is coefficientModelTorAmplitude_restricted_test_isZero and requires only restrictions of global N, never extensions of arbitrary slice test modules.

source.place: Tags 0E8K, 07A4 and 08FZ: K-flat restriction, tensor restriction and Tor vanishing.

proof.text: A module sheaf F that restricts to zero on a CoversTop family is zero. To prove its identity morphism equals zero, apply the faithful underlying-sheaf functor and test on sections over every object T. The covering sieve Sieve.ofObjects V on T consists of arrows W→T with some W→V_i. Evaluate the equality id=0 for F|V_i on that slice object to obtain id=0 on F(W). The sheaf hom_ext axiom for this covering makes id=0 on F(T). This includes an empty covering family. Apply this to every Tor-test homology sheaf from the preceding step; all representatives and global modules were arbitrary, so the chosen common interval proves global Tor amplitude.

source.place: Tags 00VH and 00VR: covering sieves and uniqueness in the sheaf condition.

from.place: Proof of det-lem-integral-models-stacks: identification of local finite Tor dimension in Stacks 09C1 with a global finite Tor interval; expanded uniformity sentence in Stacks 09C2.

split_report.summary: Preserved the arbitrary constant-coefficient statement. Proved both implications using the existing ringed-site Tor restriction theorem, exact restriction and derived tensor comparison. Uniformized bounds on finite affine refinements and proved global vanishing directly from the sheaf axiom, including the empty scheme. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes det-lem-integral-models-stacks, proof step identifying locally finite Tor dimension of the first residue reduction with a single global Tor interval, expanding the uniformity sentence of Stacks 09C2 on the integral-models route.

tool_uses.why: Its arbitrary-ringed-topos tensor comparison specializes to localization; the integral-models unit does not supply this general tensor identity.
Its arbitrary-ringed-site statement preserves a fixed interval against every slice module, for both global-to-local and refinement; the unit gives no such general restriction theorem.
The pro-etale topology, including finite affine refinement for affine targets and Zariski covers, supplies the covering facts used to uniformize bounds without a Noetherian hypothesis.

Its K-flat flat-term model of the ringed-site derived tensor identifies the tensor of the cited Tor restriction theorem with the Tor-amplitude tensor of the statement; the integral-models unit gives no tensor convention of its own.
